item.description: arXiv:2610.37858v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stochastic-gradient Langevin methods are sampling algorithms that replace the gradient of the log probability density by a noisy, possibly biased evaluation. We study how such gradient-evaluation errors affect the Euler and randomized midpoint discretizations of Langevin dynamics by comparing each noisy chain with its exact-gradient counterpart. For continuously differentiable, strongly log-concave targets with globally Lipschitz gradients, we derive comparison bounds under a sub-Gaussian condition on the gradient noise. The resulting 2-Wasserstein bounds hold uniformly over iterations, and are linear in both the step size and the $L^2$ norm of the evaluation bias, with a square-root dependence on dimensionality. To the best of our knowledge, no comparable 2-Wasserstein bounds have previously been established for randomized midpoint with noisy gradients. For Euler, our results complement recent Wasserstein bounds by allowing biased evaluations, and by not requiring additional regularity assumptions on the evaluation errors.
item.dc:creator: Yifei Xiong, Vinayak Rao

item.title: Scalable Bayesian Quadrature via Operator-Adapted Features
item.description: arXiv:2610.38212v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Kernel methods face two recurrent bottlenecks: the cubic cost of inverting an $n\times n$ kernel matrix, as in kernel ridge regression, and the evaluation of kernel integrals, as required in kernel quadrature. Existing low-rank kernel and Gaussian process approximations primarily address the former bottleneck, but do not control the downstream quadrature error when both the kernel matrix and kernel mean are approximated, particularly when the integrand lies outside the kernel reproducing kernel Hilbert space. We address both challenges through an operator-adapted finite-feature approximation. Specifically, we construct a finite-dimensional working kernel from the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of a second-order differential operator. We establish convergence guarantees for the resulting finite-feature estimators in kernel quadrature, with extension to other related kernel methods. Our results show that, with $m \lesssim n$ basis functions, the truncated estimator attains the corresponding benchmark statistical rates. The theory covers fixed/random designs, noisy/noiseless observations, oversmoothing/undersmoothing regimes, and Mat\'ern/Gaussian-type weights. We provide explicit error bounds that quantify the roles of the spectral cutoff, regularization parameter, lengthscale, sampling geometry, and operator boundary condition. We verify the convergence results in numerical experiments.
item.dc:creator: Huanyan Zhu, Cheng Li

item.title: A Hybrid Physics-informed holomorphic neural networks Method
item.description: arXiv:2610.38269v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Physics-informed holomorphic neural networks (PIHNNs) exploit complex-analytic representations to satisfy homogeneous PDEs by construction, but their extension to nonhomogeneous problems is nontrivial. We propose a hybrid physics-informed holomorphic neural network (HPIHNN) framework based on a decomposition of the solution into particular and homogeneous components. The particular component is computed by a spectral method on a simple extended domain, while the homogeneous component is approximated by a PIHNN trained only on the boundary with modified boundary data. The resulting formulation avoids meshing complex geometries and retains the dimensionality-reduction advantage of holomorphic representations. The method is applied to nonhomogeneous Poisson, Stokes, biharmonic, linear elasticity, and Helmholtz equations. Numerical experiments covering complex geometries, corner singularities, and nearly incompressible regimes demonstrate that the proposed method accurately resolves the corresponding solutions and, in the considered tests, generally achieves lower errors and shorter training times than standard PINNs. The results indicate that coupling spectral particular solutions with holomorphic neural approximations provides an efficient approach to nonhomogeneous PDEs on complex domains.
item.dc:creator: Zhijie Su, Qiaolin He, Zhiping Mao, Shiquan Zhang

item.title: Structured Pruning of Feedback Delay Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.38768v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Feedback delay networks (FDNs) are recursive filter structures used to synthesise artificial reverberation. Their feedback matrix governs both energy exchange between delay lines and the computation required at every sample, making its design central to balancing an FDN's acoustic performance and implementation efficiency. In this work, we develop an FDN-specific structured pruning method that connects these acoustic and computational concerns, allowing high-order dense orthogonal designs to be fitted to efficient implementations. The feedback matrix is replaced by stages of fixed permutations and small orthogonal blocks. We characterise connectivity growth with the network depth and derive exact conditional block updates for matrix fitting, followed by refinement against the reference FDN magnitude response. The resulting factors admit direct vectorised evaluation, with arithmetic cost and coefficient storage scaling linearly with network size for fixed block size and depth. On an Apple M2, the selected staged kernels achieve feedback-multiplication speedups over dense BLAS ranging from approximately threefold to over twentyfold across the tested network sizes, while substantially reducing coefficient storage. Objective metrics and listening tests indicate that the proposed staged approximations closely preserve the spectral and temporal character of their dense references. An analysis of processor utilisation and register reuse explains why execution time depends on more than the operation count. Finally, block size and depth provide practical control over response fidelity, storage, and real-time cost, allowing acoustic design to precede the choice of an efficient implementation.
item.dc:creator: Facundo Franchino, Karolina Prawda

item.title: Safeguarded Neurally-Accelerated Preconditioning (SNAP) framework for Nonlinear Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.38790v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce the Safeguarded Neurally-Accelerated Preconditioning (SNAP) framework for hybridizing nonlinear optimization methods with pre-trained neural operators (NOs). SNAP targets parametric optimization problems arising from variational formulations of nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs), where many parameter instances require repeated solves. Inspired by multilevel line-search methods, SNAP operates in cycles, combining classical optimization steps with a search direction generated by a pre-trained NO. Since NO-generated search directions carry no a priori descent guarantee, SNAP employs an a posteriori safeguard by accepting only corrections that satisfy prescribed descent and acceptance conditions. We prove global convergence of the SNAP algorithm and show that it preserves the convergence rate of the underlying optimization method independently of the employed NO architecture. Moreover, we also show that when the NO corrections are sufficiently accurate, SNAP converges faster, with the improvement directly related to the NO training error. To demonstrate SNAP's efficiency in practice, we run numerical experiments on a diverse set of nonlinear parametric optimization problems, including parametric minimal surface, Allen--Cahn, and nonlinear Helmholtz problems. The efficiency of SNAP is demonstrated by comparing two NO architectures, Fourier neural operator (FNO) and Transolver, and by using SNAP as a standalone solver and as a nonlinear preconditioner. Our numerical results show a substantial reduction in the number of required iterations, while demonstrating robustness and generalization across a wide range of problem parameters and mesh resolutions.
item.dc:creator: Youngkyu Lee, George Em Karniadakis, Alena Kopani\v{c}\'akov\'a

item.title: Dual Area-Volume-of-Fluid (DAVOF): co-advecting volume and face-area fractions for a closed-form, cell-local interface normal and position on unstructured meshes
item.description: arXiv:2610.38863v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Geometric Volume-of-Fluid (VOF) on unstructured polyhedral meshes reconstructs the interface orientation from the volume fractions of a stencil of neighbours; on irregular cells and in the presence of wisps it degrades, and the curvature built on it drives the parasitic currents of capillary flows. We transport, consistently to the volume fraction of every cell, the wetted fraction of every face area. From the area and volume fractions, closed-form equations recover the interface normal and position of a cell, for the first time in VOF: the normal from one sum over the cell's own faces, the divergence theorem on the liquid sub-volume, and the plane's position from a second, without neighbours or iteration. Both identities are exact for a plane on hexahedral, perturbed and polyhedral cells. On a sphere and an ellipsoid the normal has the order of the face fractions, the position is second order for every state and mesh, and a quadric through one ring of recovered normals gives a converging curvature where the reference models show none. Transported with the plane clipping, the ring normal, the same identity on the union of the cell's ring, stabilises the state and carries a sphere over 3.3 diameters bounded and conservative, first order in the face fractions as the clipping law predicts, at plicRDF's position and shape errors. A preliminary transport implementation with one paraboloid per cell, its frame from the normal, its curvature tensor from the ring and its position from the volume fraction, carries the sphere bounded and conservative over the resolution ladder with face fractions of order 2.8 per period with the exact normal and 2.1 with the ring quadric's normal over N = 32 to 128. The loop has the order of the normal it is fed; a transported normal of second order is the research goal. This document is the basis on which the further development of the method is documented.
item.dc:creator: Tomislav Mari\'c

item.title: Exponential-Nemytskii Neural Operators: Learning Field Evolution Across Step Sizes
item.description: arXiv:2610.39041v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In variable-step operator learning, agreement at observed step sizes does not by itself determine predictions at other temporal resolutions. We propose an operator whose step-size dependence is prescribed by a first-order Duhamel approximation of semilinear dynamics. It combines exact linear propagation with a local nonlinear function of the field and its derivatives, allowing evaluation below the observation interval without supervision densely sampled across step sizes. Under suitable conditions and at fixed spatial resolution, we prove that agreement between models at two step sizes controls their prediction differences throughout a prescribed range. We also give conditions for local identifiability of both components from two step sizes, supporting interpretation of the learned structure. A latent extension applies the same construction to learned fields. We evaluate the base model on two synthetic problems and the extension on two real datasets against several baselines.
item.dc:creator: Jingye Li, Jinglai Li

item.title: Finding solutions with the Borsuk-Ulam theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.39092v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many existence theorems in combinatorics and geometry reduce to the Borsuk-Ulam theorem or its generalizations. We study how these existence arguments can be turned into effective numerical methods when a simple example with a single known solution is available. The idea is to deform this example into the given problem and follow its solution during the deformation. We establish conditions under which this procedure reaches a solution and estimate the work needed for a prescribed accuracy. Mass partition problems illustrate the method for both continuous objects and finite point sets. In a fixed dimension, each step for point sets requires work proportional to the number of points; we give conditions under which the entire computation has this linear cost. We also study how changing the initial example can lead to other solutions and support a search for all of them.
item.dc:creator: Oleg R. Musin

item.title: Convergence of Levenberg--Marquardt method in Banach spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.39131v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the Levenberg--Marquardt method for nonlinear inverse problems in Banach spaces under a H\"{o}lder stability estimate. Under suitable assumptions on the geometry of the Banach space and the Fr\'{e}chet derivative of the measurement operator, we establish the well-definedness of the method, local convergence and convergence rates for exact data, and the monotonic decrease of the Bregman distance up to the stopping index for noisy data. These results extend the corresponding Hilbert space theory to the Banach space setting.
item.dc:creator: Akari Ishida, Sei Nagayasu

item.title: Linearize or Discretize First? Error Estimates under Mesh-Uniform Regularity and Exponential Stability for the KdV Equation with Boundary Dissipation
item.description: arXiv:2610.39269v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation, and its spatial semidiscretization by a weighted cubic Hermite Galerkin method. A small nonlinear wave can be approximated by a linear discrete simulation in two orders: linearize first and then discretize, or discretize first and then linearize. Both orders give the same total error, but they divide it differently between linearization and discretization. The difference of the two divisions is the ordering error. We show that it is quadratic in the size of the initial datum and carries a positive power of the mesh size, for all time. For the continuous problem, the solution map is analytic, with a power series that converges for all time in exponentially weighted trajectory norms. The linearized semigroup has Crandall-Pazy regularity with the exact index 3/2. For the weighted scheme, exponential stability, Kato smoothing, Crandall-Pazy regularity and analyticity of the solution maps hold uniformly in the mesh size. These properties give error estimates in which the error and the datum are measured in the same norm: in the energy norm, in $H_0^1$ and in $H^2$. In exponentially weighted time-integrated norms the semidiscrete solutions converge uniformly on balls, at the rate $h^{1/6}$ in $L^4(0,\infty;L^2)$ for data in $L^2$ and at the rate $h^{2/3}$ in $L^2(0,\infty;H^1)$ for data in $H_0^1$. On every interval $[t_0,\infty)$, $t_0>0$, same-norm convergence holds uniformly on balls at algebraic rates. The ordering error is of order $h^{1/6}$ times the square of the energy norm of the datum, uniformly for all $t\ge0$. For the unweighted scheme, a grid wave packet of zero group velocity destroys mesh-uniform Kato smoothing and Crandall-Pazy regularity.
item.dc:creator: Kangsheng Liu

item.title: Data-driven Random-feature Approximation of Koopman Generators of Nonlinear Continuous-time Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.39897v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learning continuous-time dynamical systems from data is an active area of research. The Koopman formalism is often used here, because it is a flexible approach that is informative about the system's fundamental properties. The formalism represents dynamical systems through linear operators acting on a suitable function space. A practical difficulty arising in the numerical approximation of Koopman operators is the choice of a ``dictionary'', meaning an effective finite-dimensional representation of the function space. In this paper, we focus on learning dynamical systems in continuous-time, and so we consider numerical approximations of the Koopman generator instead of the Koopman operator. Our main contribution is a data-driven random-feature method to obtain a parsimonious and effective function representation for Galerkin approximation methods such as gEDMD. The representation we construct is data-informed, which allows us to improve upon data-agnostic methods. We empirically demonstrate the suitability of our method for forecasting tasks and system analysis. The numerical experiments show that our approach is accurate, and faster than iterative optimization. Further, we prove convergence of our approximation of the vector field and the resulting trajectories. In addition to the numerical results, we also make theoretical contributions, including a general convergence criterion for the semigroup generated by the gEDMD approximation and a counterexample showing that gEDMD does not generally preserve exponential boundedness. With our contribution, we advance the frontier of efficiently learning continuous-time dynamics from data, towards interpretable and mathematically robust modelling based on the Koopman framework.
item.dc:creator: Ana \v{C}ukarska, Maximilian Gollwitzer, Viola Muning Li, Vladyslav Fediukov, Zahra Monfared, Felix Dietrich

item.title: Numerical Investigation of Soft-to-Hard Convergence: Discretization, Admissibility, and Spectral Regularity
item.description: arXiv:2610.40461v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper presents a numerical investigation of soft-to-hard terminal constraint convergence for optimal control problems governed by a second-order ordinary differential equation and the one-dimensional heat equation. The study complements the analytical convergence theory through comparisons with exact solutions and independently computed numerical approximations. For the heat equation, a fully discrete Crank--Nicolson finite-difference formulation is validated against exact modal solutions, exhibiting approximately second-order convergence in the terminal-state and midpoint-sampled control errors under simultaneous space-time mesh refinement. Numerical experiments demonstrate the predicted first-order penalty convergence for benchmark problems and investigate the admissibility threshold governing finite-energy exact terminal controllability. Additional modal experiments examine the dependence of terminal-error convergence rates on spectral regularity, illustrating intermediate rates consistent with the theoretical estimates and asymptotic predictions. The results provide computational evidence supporting the soft-to-hard convergence framework and clarify the roles of discretization, target admissibility, and spectral regularity.
item.dc:creator: Sung-Sik Kwon, Marcus Nunda

item.title: On a mixed FEM and a FOSLS with $H^{-1}$ loads
item.description: arXiv:2210.14063v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study variants of the mixed finite element method (mixed FEM) and the first-order system least-squares finite element (FOSLS) for the Poisson problem where we replace the load by a suitable regularization which permits to use $H^{-1}$ loads. We prove that any bounded $H^{-1}$ projector onto piecewise constants can be used to define the regularization and yields quasi-optimality of the lowest-order mixed FEM resp. FOSLS in weaker norms. Examples for the construction of such projectors are given. One is based on the adjoint of a weighted Cl\'ement quasi-interpolator. We prove that this Cl\'ement operator has second-order approximation properties. For the modified mixed method we show optimal convergence rates of a postprocessed solution under minimal regularity assumptions -- a result not valid for the lowest-order mixed FEM without regularization. Numerical examples conclude this work.
item.dc:creator: Thomas F\"uhrer

item.title: A continuous scale space of diffeomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2501.04031v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we define and study a nested family of reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces of vector fields that is indexed by a range of scales, from which we construct a reproducing kernel Hilbert space of scale-dependent vector fields. We provide a characterization of the reproducing kernel of that space, with numerical approximations ensuring quick evaluations when this kernel does not have a closed form. We then introduce a multiscale version of the large deformation diffeomorphic metric mapping (LDDMM) problem and prove the existence of solutions. Finally, we provide numerical experiments performing landmark matching using multiscale LDDMM.
item.dc:creator: Yechen Liu, Laurent Younes

item.title: Deep neural network approximation for high-dimensional parabolic partial integro-differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2501.10880v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we investigate the existence of a deep neural network (DNN) capable of approximating solutions to partial integro-differential equations while circumventing the curse of dimensionality. Using the Feynman-Kac theorem, we express the solution in terms of stochastic differential equations (SDEs). Based on several properties of classical estimators, we establish the existence of a DNN that satisfies the necessary assumptions. The results are theoretical and don't have any numerical experiments yet.
item.dc:creator: Marcin Baranek

item.title: Hierarchical Matrices with Tucker Blocks: Construction and Forward Evaluation
item.description: arXiv:2508.05958v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we introduce hierarchical matrices with Tucker blocks (HMTB) for data-sparse approximation of matrices arising from nonoscillatory and mildly oscillatory kernels. Building on the hierarchical matrix framework, HMTB matrices replace conventional low-rank blocks with Tucker representations. Using high-dimensional interpolation and tensor compression and contractions, we develop algorithms for constructing HMTB matrices and performing matrix-vector multiplication. For an $N \times N$ matrix, these algorithms have linear and quasi-linear complexities in $N$, respectively. Numerical comparisons with an interpolation-based $\mathcal{H}$-matrix implementation demonstrate storage savings and, in several cases, reduced construction times, while maintaining competitive forward-evaluation costs. The framework is also applicable to quasi-uniform grids.
item.dc:creator: Yingzhou Li, Jingyu Liu

item.title: Quasi-Trefftz spaces for a second order time-harmonic Maxwell's equation
item.description: arXiv:2509.00193v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quasi-Trefftz methods are a family of Discontinuous Galerkin methods relying on equation-dependent function spaces. This work is the first study of the notion of local Taylor-based polynomial quasi-Trefftz spaces for a system of Partial Differential Equations (PDEs). These discrete spaces are meant to discretize a quasi-Trefftz weak formulation, and are introduced here for electro-magnetic wave propagation in inhomogeneous media, governed by a second order formulation of Maxwell's equation with variable coefficients. Thanks to an adequate Helmholtz decomposition for spaces of homogeneous polynomial vector fields, the outcome is the proposed quasi-Trefftz spaces with same best approximation properties as the corresponding standard polynomial spaces but with an optimal dimension, as well as a procedure to construct a quasi-Trefftz basis.
item.dc:creator: Ilaria Fontana, Lise-Marie Imbert-G\'erard

item.title: Data-driven model order reduction for wave propagation in materials with damage and nonlinearities
item.description: arXiv:2511.20815v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we consider wave propagation in materials characterized by nonlinear properties or damage. To accelerate the simulations of the resulting high-dimensional problems, we apply model order reduction methods. Depending on the knowledge of the underlying equations and the availability of their discrete operators, intrusive methods (here projection-based approaches based on proper orthogonal decomposition (POD)) or non-instrusive methods (here data-driven approaches including dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) and operator inference (OpInf)) can be used. We recall the theoretical foundations of the methods and apply them to the problem of wave propagation. In three different numerical examples, we evaluate the performance of the reduction techniques.
item.dc:creator: Saddam Hijazi, Nikiema Fulgence, Hannah Burmester, Natalie Rauter, Carmen Gr\"a{\ss}le

item.title: Stochstic Sampling for Generative Diffusion Models: From Euler-Maruyama to Higher-Order Schemes
item.description: arXiv:2601.18425v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a convergence analysis for generative diffusion models that simultaneously accounts for the three principal error sources in stochastic sampling: initialization, score matching, and discretization of the reverse-time stochastic differential equation (SDE). Our central tool is the notion of a iterative-wise general strong scheme, a broad class of discretization methods for the reverse dynamics defined via explicit, index-wise tolerances on their It\^o--Taylor coefficients. This notion refines Kloeden and Platen's general strong schemes into an iterate-wise formulation whose per-step conditions imply the classical remainder bound. We prove a 2-Wasserstein convergence theorem that applies to this entire class, reducing the analysis of any concrete sampler to a finite checklist, and covers general forward processes with time-dependent, spatially linear drift and spatially independent diffusion coefficient. We focus on dissipative reverse-time SDEs, which allows us to relax the $T$-dependence of the discretization and score-matching errors from exponential to polynomial. We instantiate our theorem for Euler--Maruyama, the exponential integrator, and, as our main application, derivative-free stochastic Runge--Kutta schemes of strong order $1.5$. To our knowledge, these are the first full convergence guarantees for solvers whose strong order strictly exceeds that of Euler--Maruyama. We further derive the resulting iteration complexity and a parameter-selection rule for the terminal time, score accuracy, and step size. Numerical experiments on Gaussian toy models and CIFAR-10 are consistent with the predicted convergence orders, and on ImageNet, out-of-the-box higher-order SDE solvers can yield substantial speed-ups, requiring at least four times fewer score evaluations than Euler--Maruyama. Code available at: https://github.com/emanuelpfarr/SSGDM.
item.dc:creator: Emanuel Pfarr, Radu Timofte, Frank Werner

item.title: Worst-case $L_p$-approximation of periodic functions using median lattice algorithms
item.description: arXiv:2603.05271v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the worst-case approximation of multivariate periodic functions from the weighted Korobov space $H_{d,\alpha,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}$ with smoothness $\alpha>1/2$ and weights $\boldsymbol{\gamma}$ in the Lebesgue norm $L_p([0,1]^d)$ for $1\le p\le\infty$. We analyze a \emph{median lattice algorithm} that reconstructs a truncated Fourier series by approximating the coefficients on a hyperbolic-cross-type index set using $R$ rank-1 lattice sampling rules with independent randomly chosen generating vectors, and then aggregating the resulting coefficient estimators via the componentwise median. For an odd number of repetitions $R$ and an odd prime lattice size $N$, where $R$ depends logarithmically on $N$, we prove high-probability error bounds in both $L_\infty$ and $L_2$. Interpolation then yields the result for all $ p \in [1,\infty]$. In particular, with high probability, the worst-case $L_p$-error satisfies, for any $\beta>0$, an upper bound of the following form \[ \ C_{d,\alpha,\beta,\boldsymbol{\gamma},\tau,p}\,R^{\frac{1}{2}+(\frac12 - \frac1p)_+} N^{- \alpha + (\frac12 - \frac1p)_+ + \beta }, \] where $(x)_+ = \max\{x, 0\}$, and the constant $C_{d,\alpha,\beta,\boldsymbol{\gamma},\tau,p}$ is independent of $N$ and $R$. For $p=\infty$, $C_{d,\alpha,\beta,\boldsymbol{\gamma},\tau,\infty}$ is dimension-independent under the summability condition $\sum_{j=1}^\infty \gamma_j^{1/(2\alpha)}<\infty$. These results extend recent analyses of median-based lattice approximation in $L_2$ and complement related multiple-shift lattice approaches, showing that median aggregation yields nearly optimal $L_p$-approximation rates (up to logarithmic factors and an arbitrarily small loss) in weighted Korobov spaces.
item.dc:creator: Zexin Pan, Mou Cai, Josef Dick, Takashi Goda, Peter Kritzer

item.title: Minimum residual discretization of a semilinear elliptic problem
item.description: arXiv:2603.29863v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a least-squares penalization as a means to extend the discontinuous Petrov-Galerkin (DPG) method with optimal test functions to a class of semilinear elliptic problems. The nonlinear contributions are replaced with independent unknowns so that standard DPG techniques apply to the resulting linear problem with non-trivial kernel. The nonlinear relations are added as least-squares constraints. Assuming solvability of the semilinear problem and an Aubin--Nitsche-type approximation property for the primal variable, we prove a C\'ea estimate for the approximation error in canonical norms. We also give conditions ensuring unique solvability and, under additional regularity and stability assumptions, derive the required nonlinear Aubin-Nitsche estimate. Numerical results with uniform and adaptively refined meshes illustrate the performance of the scheme, also in comparison with the Gauss-Newton approach.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Garc\'ia Vera, Norbert Heuer, Dirk Praetorius

item.title: High-order parametric local discontinuous Galerkin methods for anisotropic curve-shortening flows
item.description: arXiv:2604.03106v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a family of high-order local discontinuous Galerkin (LDG) methods, built on a parametric representation and coupled with a semi-implicit backward Euler time discretization, for isotropic and anisotropic curve-shortening flows. The spatial LDG formulation introduces auxiliary variables and carefully designed numerical fluxes which inherit the underlying variational structure. We prove unconditional energy dissipation for the semidiscrete scheme and establish energy dissipation and well-posedness for the fully discrete scheme under certain assumptions. For $P^k$ approximations, the LDG method achieves high-order spatial convergence; extensive numerical experiments confirm optimal $(k+1)$-order accuracy when the surface energy is isotropic or weakly anisotropic. Compared to classical parametric finite element methods (PFEM), the proposed LDG schemes do not need to rely on good mesh distributions or auxiliary symmetrized surface energy matrices for strongly anisotropic surface energy cases, and remain numerically stable on severely degraded meshes that typically cause PFEMs failure. This intrinsic stability enables effective capture of complex geometric evolution and sharp corner singularities produced by strong anisotropy. The approach thus provides a flexible and reliable framework for the numerical simulation of a broader class of geometric flows.
item.dc:creator: Xiuhui Guo, Wei Jiang, Chunmei Su

item.title: Evaluation of Gauss-Legendre curves
item.description: arXiv:2604.17331v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present new representations of Gauss--Legendre polynomials and their derivatives in the shifted power basis and in bases related to symmetric orthogonal Jacobi polynomials. Using these representations and certain recurrence relations, we propose $O(n^2+dn)$ methods for evaluating a Gauss--Legendre curve of degree $n$ in $\mathbb E^d$. We also propose algorithms for multipoint evaluation with computational complexity $O(Mdn+dn^2)$, where $M$ is the number of evaluation points. Numerical tests show that the approach using the shifted power basis is very fast, but it works well only for small $n$ (approximately up to 20), whereas the method employing Jacobi polynomials gives good numerical results even for large $n$ (around 100).
item.dc:creator: Filip Chudy, Pawe{\l} Wo\'zny

item.title: A neural network method for scalar conservation laws with convergence rates for shock waves
item.description: arXiv:2604.27458v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a new entropy-compatible neural network method for scalar hyperbolic conservation laws and establish, to our knowledge, the first explicit $L^1$ convergence rates in this setting for piecewise smooth entropy solutions, including those with discontinuities. The method is based on a computable approximation of the Kru\v{z}kov entropy residual that sits between the strong and weak forms of the entropy inequality. For a single regular shock in one dimension and finitely many smooth shock hypersurfaces with transversal interactions in several dimensions, we construct explicit neural networks with provably small loss by combining shock-adapted continuous piecewise linear functions with known approximation properties of $\tanh$ neural networks. The one-dimensional analysis also covers rarefactions, compound waves, regular shock interactions, and nondegenerate shock formation from smooth initial data. Together with entropy-based stability estimates, this gives rigorous $L^1$ error bounds for minimizers of the proposed loss. In particular, when the network size grows in proportion to the number of degrees of freedom of a space--time mesh of size $h$, the analysis recovers the classical Kuznetsov rate $O(h^{1/2})$ in shock-dominated cases. Numerical experiments in one and two space dimensions illustrate the performance of the method.
item.dc:creator: Jiachuan Cao, Buyang Li, Hao Li

item.title: A novel class of high-order uniformly accurate exponential integrators with local linear extension for the charged-particle dynamics under strong magnetic field
item.description: arXiv:2606.04478v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we develop a novel class of high-order uniformly accurate exponential integrators for charged-particle dynamics under strong magnetic field. The small parameter $0<\varepsilon\ll 1$ induces rapid temporal oscillations, rendering traditional numerical methods prohibitively expensive due to severe step-size restrictions. To address this issue, a linearization technology that introduces auxiliary polynomial variables is employed to recast the original charged-particle dynamics as a higher-dimensional system. Classical exponential integrators are subsequently applied to this augmented formulation, which inherently carries richer structural information, thereby yielding a family of uniformly accurate exponential integrators that can reach arbitrarily high order without requiring any order conditions. For strong magnetic fields under the maximal-ordering scaling, we rigorously establish through algebraic techniques that the schemes with auxiliary polynomial variables of degree $k\geq2$ achieve an improved position error bound of $\mathcal{O}(\min\{\varepsilon^{k+1}h,\varepsilon h^{k+1}\})$ and a uniform velocity error bound of $\mathcal{O}(\min\{\varepsilon^{k}h,h^{k+1}\})$, where $h$ denotes the time-step size. Under the additional condition that the magnetic field gradient vanishes at the origin, these bounds sharpen to $\mathcal{O}(\min\{\varepsilon^{k+2},\varepsilon h^{k+1}\})$ and $\mathcal{O}(\min\{\varepsilon^{k+1},h^{k+1}\})$ for the position and velocity, respectively, for $k\geq1$. The same sharper bounds hold for constant strong magnetic fields. Numerical experiments confirm the advantages of the proposed methods.
item.dc:creator: Lina Wang, Bin Wang, Beibei Zhu

item.title: Dual Gauss--Legendre polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2606.11355v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define and investigate two families of dual polynomials associated with the Gauss--Legendre polynomials, which have recently found interesting applications in computer graphics. Using the presented results, one can derive representations of the Gauss--Legendre polynomials, construct the dual bases for Lagrange bases and solve certain approximation problems arising, for example, in CAGD.
item.dc:creator: Pawe{\l} Wo\'zny

item.title: Hypocoercivity-preserving space-time Galerkin methods for kinetic Fokker-Planck equations
item.description: arXiv:2606.29621v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We design and analyse a family of hypocoercivity-preserving fully discrete Galerkin methods for the kinetic Fokker--Planck (kFP) equations, a class of evolution partial differential equations (PDE) with \emph{degenerate} diffusion. The key idea in the method design is to mimic the framework of enhanced quadratic forms of Villani \cite{villani} to obtain a coercive bilinear form in a sufficiently strong exponentially weighted norm admitting a spectral gap/Poincar\'{e} inequality, despite the degeneracy. The problem is posed as a fourth-order evolution PDE on the whole space $\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^d$. The spatial discretization employs continuous piecewise polynomial approximation spaces on simplicial and/or box-type meshes comprising finite and infinite elements. Nonconformity is treated by constructing appropriate numerical fluxes in the spirit of $C^0$-interior penalty ($C^0$-IP) methods for fourth-order elliptic problems. The proof of coercivity requires new trace inverse inequalities for exponentially weighted norms on $d$-dimensional simplicial and box-type domains, and prismatic domains with infinite length. We prove these inequalities for a variety of exponential weights. Once coercivity is established, exponential convergence to equilibrium follows from an exponentially weighted Poincar\'{e} inequality. A fully discrete extension is obtained by coupling the spatial discretization with an $hp$-version discontinuous Galerkin time-stepping scheme. Exponential convergence to equilibrium is also proven for the fully discrete scheme. The proposed methods preserve total mass and exhibit \emph{provably} exponential convergence to equilibrium, a manifestation of `numerical hypocoercivity,' making them well suited for long-time kFP simulations. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical results and investigate the convergence behaviour of the proposed method.
item.dc:creator: Zhaonan Dong, Emmanuil H. Georgoulis

item.title: A family of mixed-mixed strongly conservative finite element methods for Biot's model of consolidation
item.description: arXiv:2607.16418v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a four-field formulation of Biot's quasi-static model of consolidation with the (effective) elastic stress, the solid displacement, the fluid flux and the fluid pressure as unknown physical quantities of interest. The weak form of this system composed of the momentum and mass balance equations complemented by the stress-strain relation and Darcy's law yields a two-fold perturbed saddle-point problem. Its well-posedness is proven for a natural choice of inifinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, where the displacement-flux pair is sought in a novel Hilbert space. Next, based on recent works on $H(\rm div \, \rm div)$-conforming finite elements, we propose a family of mixed-mixed finite element methods that preserve the angular momentum as well as the fluid mass balance pointwise, i.e., in a strong sense. We prove the well-posedness of the arising discrete problem and establish optimal a priori error estimates for the related family of fully conservative mixed-mixed finite element methods.
item.dc:creator: Qingguo Hong, Johannes Kraus, Maria Lymbery

item.title: Analysis and structure-preserving discretization of the Heat-GLM system
item.description: arXiv:2607.22151v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study a prototype hyperbolic system arising from the coupling of Generalized-Lagrangian-Multiplier (GLM) curl-cleaning with linear acoustics. We first show that, in the absence of dissipation, the equations can be rigorously derived from an underlying variational principle and that the resulting system is symmetric-hyperbolic. Further analysis shows that it not only conserves the total energy but also admits a set of invariants consisting of quadratic combinations of differential operators applied to the state variables. The addition of a stiff relaxation source term allows the system to be extended to dissipative dynamics, describing, for example, Cattaneo-type heat transfer processes that are asymptotically compatible with the Fourier law in the stiff relaxation limit; in this case, the total energy and invariants are dissipated accordingly. A new semi-implicit compatible numerical scheme on staggered grids is developed to solve this system while exactly preserving its key properties at the discrete level. In particular, we prove that the scheme is asymptotic-preserving in the Fourier limit, with a convergence rate depending on the initial data. We also show that the scheme conserves exactly the total energy as well as all the invariants in the absence of relaxation, and dissipates them consistently in its presence. These findings are demonstrated on a set of representative test cases.
item.dc:creator: Firas Dhaouadi, Laura R\'io-Mart\'in, Michael Dumbser

item.title: A GPU-Accelerated Blocked Adaptive Randomized Range Finder Based on an Implicit Householder QR Decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2608.28941v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Low-rank methods can reduce the memory and computational requirements of deep neural network training in approaches such as GaLore. Randomized range finders offer an attractive alternative to singular value decompositions, particularly when the required rank is determined adaptively from a prescribed approximation tolerance. We introduce a blocked adaptive randomized range finder based on a Householder QR decomposition and an optimized hybrid CPU--GPU implementation. Numerical experiments show that it preserves orthogonality and approximation accuracy in regimes where block Gram--Schmidt without reorthogonalization becomes unstable. The blocked formulation exposes matrix--matrix operations and enables overlap of CPU panel factorization with GPU updates. On an NVIDIA GH200, the overlapped implementation reduces the runtime for the largest tested matrix from 9.91 s on the CPU to 0.407 s. The method provides a stable and efficient building block for low-rank approximation on heterogeneous systems with applications in computational science and engineering.
item.dc:creator: Carolin Penke, Andreas Herten

item.title: Constraints on admissible behavior of GMRES applied to tridiagonal Toeplitz systems
item.description: arXiv:2609.24751v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The result of Greenbaum, Pt\'ak, and Strako\v{s} that for a given set of eigenvalues, any convergence curve is possible [SIMAX 1996] and the subsequent parameterization of such matrix-right-hand side pairs $(A,\mathbf{b})$ of Arioli, Pt\'ak, and Strako\v{s} [BIT 1998] demonstrated that the behavior of the GMRES could not be completely characterized by the eigenvalues of $A$ alone. In this paper, we consider how to use this theory to understand the admissible and attainable \gmres behavior for matrices with constrained structure, focussing on non-Hermitian (non-symmetric) tridiagonal Toeplitz matrices. We show that Toeptliz structure necessarily constrains the how the theory from these papers can manifest but that a continuum of admissible behaviors is still attainable.
item.dc:creator: Fei Chen, Kirk M. Soodhalter

item.title: Flow Matching for Fast Posterior Sampling in Bayesian Inverse Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.02377v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Sampling from the posterior is the central task of computational Bayesian inverse problems. The standard workhorse in Bayesian inference---Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC)---is sequential, yields correlated samples, and must be rerun for each new observation. Conditional flow matching offers an amortized alternative: a transport map, trained once on joint samples of parameter and data, that yields independent approximate posterior samples for any observation at negligible online cost, without new likelihood evaluations. We give a careful, MCMC-literate assessment of flow matching for PDE-based inverse problems with function-valued parameters. Exploiting the flow's tractable density, we derive computable accuracy estimates for the learned posterior in total variation distance and Kullback--Leibler divergence and, moreover, propose a hybrid sampler that is made asymptotically exact by Metropolization. We validate the accuracy estimates and demonstrate amortization in several numerical examples, including electrical impedance tomography and a likelihood-free Lotka--Volterra model. Flow matching reproduces posterior means and credible bands closely at a fraction of the forward solves required by MCMC, but its accuracy degrades for concentrated posteriors and for observations that are atypical under the prior.
item.dc:creator: Jan Blechschmidt, Oliver G. Ernst, Moritz Poguntke, Bj\"orn Sprungk

item.title: Hybridizable Discontinuous Galerkin methods for the Keller-Segel model
item.description: arXiv:2610.33260v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) finite element method to approximate the solution of the time-dependent Keller-Segel model, a drift-diffusion system describing chemotactic cell movement. We develop and analyze the corresponding HDG scheme, and establish theoretical convergence results for the proposed discretization. Finally, we present numerical experiments that confirm the theoretical findings.
item.dc:creator: Silvia Bertoluzza, Gabriella Bretti, Micol Pennacchio, Christophe Prud'homme

item.title: An unconditionally convergent BDF2-type finite element integrator for the inertial Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.35382v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose and analyze a fully discrete numerical scheme to approximate solutions to the inertial Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (iLLG) equation, a state-of-the-art model to describe the dynamics of the magnetization at subpicosecond time scales. The method employs first-order finite elements for the spatial discretization and the two-step backward differentiation formula (BDF2) for the time discretization, where the inertial term is treated by a convex combination of BDF2 and the backward Euler method. We prove well-posedness and unconditional stability of the scheme, and obtain explicit bounds for the error in the realization of the iLLG-inherent unit length constraint satisfied by the magnetization. Moreover, we derive the discrete energy law satisfied by the approximations, which resembles the inherent dissipative energy law of the model. Finally, with a constructive approach, we prove unconditional convergence of the approximations toward a weak solution of the problem. Numerical experiments assess the performance of the scheme and validate the theoretical findings.
item.dc:creator: Michele Ald\'e, Hywel Normington, Dirk Praetorius, Michele Ruggeri

item.title: Monte Carlo Power Iteration Algorithms: Convergence, Analysis and Application to Reactor Criticality Calculations
item.description: arXiv:2610.36266v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Monte Carlo power iteration algorithms in the context of reactor criticality simulations. Under mild conditions on the underlying physical system and the algorithmic structure, we derive explicit error bounds, which are to the best of our knowledge the first rigorous results for such methods which are ubiquitous in nuclear engineering. This is done by exploiting connections to Sequential Monte Carlo algorithms, and extending recent developments about stochastic neutron transport. We demonstrate the applicability of our results by considering a concrete version of the Monte Carlo power iteration algorithm as well as variance reduction schemes.
item.dc:creator: Alexander M. G. Cox, Tom Davis, Julian Hofstadler, Andreas E. Kyprianou

item.title: Fast subdivision of B\'{e}zier curves
item.description: arXiv:2509.15691v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It is well-known that a $d$-dimensional polynomial B\'{e}zier curve of degree $n$ can be subdivided into two segments using the famous de Casteljau algorithm in $O(dn^2)$ time. We show that it is possible to do this in $O(dn\log{n})$ time using the fast Fourier transform and its inverse. The direct application of the method is numerically unstable for larger values of $n$. Therefore, we also introduce a modified version based on parameter scaling, which retains the same asymptotic computational complexity. This scaling approach can improve numerical accuracy in some cases (for $n\lesssim 50$), as demonstrated by our experiments. Moreover, the new method has a nice property: if a B\'{e}zier curve is extended by an additional control point, the subdivision can be updated in $O(d)$ time. The method can be adapted to subdivide rational B\'{e}zier curves and rectangular B\'{e}zier surfaces, as well as to compute the derivatives of B\'{e}zier curves. Although motivated by applications in CAGD, the proposed methods may also be useful in other areas involving polynomial reparameterization.
item.dc:creator: Pawe{\l} Wo\'zny, Filip Chudy

item.title: Inequalities, identities, and bounds for divided differences of the exponential function
item.description: arXiv:2510.10724v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\exp[x_0,x_1,\dots,x_n]$ denote the divided difference of the exponential function. (i) We prove that exponential divided differences, as functions of two nodes of arbitrary positive multiplicities with all other nodes fixed, are strictly sign-regular of all orders, with log-submodularity as the order-two case. We also establish strict supermodularity. (ii) We establish the four-point inequality $ \exp[a,a,b,c]\,\exp[d,d,b,c]+\exp[b,b,a,d]\,\exp[c,c,a,d]-\exp[a,b,c,d]^2 > 0 $ for all $ a,b,c,d \in \mathbb{R} $. Furthermore, we obtain a sharp quantitative generalization to arbitrarily many pairs of nodes, with additional common nodes allowed. (iii) We obtain sharp two-sided bounds for $\exp[x_0,\dots,x_n]$ at fixed mean and variance; as a consequence, we derive an asymptotic expansion for $n!\exp[x_0,\ldots,x_n]$ as $n\to\infty$ for node sequences of bounded variance. (iv) We present closed-form identities for divided differences of the exponential function, including a convolution identity and summation formulas for repeated arguments.
item.dc:creator: Qiulin Zeng, Nic Ezzell, Arman Babakhani, Itay Hen, Lev Barash

item.title: Quantum-inspired space-time PDE solver and dynamic mode decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2510.21767v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The numerical solution of time-dependent PDEs posed over the combined space-time domain, instead of treating time sequentially, leads to space-time methods. Treating time as another spatial dimension allows parallelization across time and simultaneous adaptivity in spatial and temporal discretizations. However, space-time formulations suffer from the curse of dimensionality due to the (d+1)-dimensional domain. Time-series forecasting methods, such as dynamic mode decomposition (DMD), also suffer the same scaling for storing and processing measurement data. In this work, we investigate whether quantum-inspired tensor network methods can mitigate this curse for both solving PDEs and data-driven modeling. We formulate a space-time matrix product state (MPS) encoding to represent either the space-time solution or time-series data. Using this representation, we develop a unified framework that combines an MPS space-time PDE solver with an MPS-DMD algorithm. We benchmark our MPS space-time solver for linear and nonlinear PDEs in both (1+1) and (2+1) dimensions, including non-diffusive regimes such as shockwave formation and Allen-Cahn phase separation. We observe that the MPS ansatz efficiently captures the spatio-temporal correlations of the solutions, with a 99% reduction in parameters with respect to the grid size. We demonstrate the MPS-DMD algorithm in two cases. First, the MPS space-time solver generates the MPS encoding of the time-series data. We then apply MPS-DMD directly to predict the dynamics without solving PDEs. Second, for the general case where data is available as dense arrays, MPS-DMD needs an intermediate compression step. We implement a streaming-like compression algorithm and observe a 97% reduction in memory, with MPS-DMD predictions matching those of exact DMD.
item.dc:creator: Raghavendra Dheeraj Peddinti, Stefano Pisoni, Narsimha Rapaka, Yacine Addad, Mohamed K. Riahi, Egor Tiunov, Leandro Aolita

item.title: Complete Characterizations of Well-Posedness in Parametric Composite Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2512.14124v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper characterizes the well-posedness of Karush-Kuhn-Tucker system for perturbed composite optimization. Using the parabolic regularity, we introduce a novel second-order variational function, shown to be the pivotal object governing second-order behavior. This foundational result yields the strong second-order sufficient condition introduced here for the general class of composite optimization problems to naturally extend the classical second-order sufficient condition in nonlinear programming. Then we obtain several equivalent characterizations of the second-order qualification condition (SOQC) and highlight its relationship with the constraint nondegeneracy condition under the $\mathcal{C}^{2}$-cone reducibility assumption. These insights lead us to multiple equivalent conditions for the major Lipschitz-like/Aubin property of KKT systems, including SOQC combined with the new second-order subdifferential condition and SOQC combined with tilt stability of local minimizers. Under the $\mathcal{C}^{2}$-cone reducibility, we settle the long-standing question by proving the equivalence between the Aubin property of KKT systems around local minimizers and the classical notion of strong regularity. Finally, we demonstrate that the Lipschitz-like property is equivalent to the nonsingularity of the generalized Jacobian associated with the KKT system under a certain verifiable assumption. These results provide a unified and rigorous framework for analyzing stability and sensitivity of solutions to composite optimization problems, as well as for the design and justification of numerical algorithms.
item.dc:creator: Boris S. Mordukhovich, Peipei Tang, Chengjing Wang

item.title: Multigrade Neural Network Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2601.16884v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study multigrade deep learning (MGDL) as a principled framework for structured error refinement in deep neural networks. While the approximation power of neural networks is now relatively well understood, training very deep architectures remains challenging due to highly nonconvex and often ill-conditioned optimization landscapes. In contrast, for relatively shallow networks, most notably certain one-hidden-layer ReLU models, training admits convex reformulations with global guarantees under appropriate settings, motivating learning paradigms that improve stability while scaling to depth. MGDL builds on this insight by training deep networks grade by grade: previously learned grades are frozen, and each newly added grade-wise subnetwork is composed on top of the previously learned grades and trained to fit the residual left by the current approximation, yielding a structured and interpretable hierarchical refinement process. We develop an operator-theoretic foundation for MGDL and prove that, for any continuous target function defined on a hypercube, there exists a fixed-width multigrade ReLU scheme whose residuals are pointwise nonincreasing in magnitude and converge uniformly to zero, with strict $L^p$-norm decay at every nontrivial grade for $p\in [1,\infty)$. To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first rigorous constructive approximation guarantee showing that a grade-wise residual refinement scheme can achieve vanishing error in a fixed-width multigrade ReLU architecture.
item.dc:creator: Shijun Zhang, Zuowei Shen, Yuesheng Xu

item.title: Stochastic Dimension Implicit Functional Projections for Global Integral Conservation in High-Dimensional PINNs
item.description: arXiv:2603.29237v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Enforcing prescribed global integral constraints in mesh-free neural PDE solvers is challenging in high-dimensional domains. Existing projection methods for spatial integrals are often tied to fixed grids or uniform quadrature, which can conflict with randomly sampled physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and scale poorly with dimension. High-order differential operators also increase reverse-mode automatic differentiation memory costs. We propose Stochastic Dimension Implicit Functional Projection (SDIFP), a quadrature-level framework for enforcing prescribed first and second spatial moments. SDIFP replaces tensor-product nodal projection by a global affine correction of the neural-network output, with two scalar coefficients determined from a weighted quadrature rule. Under positive target variance and nonzero empirical raw variance, this correction is the nearest-point projection, in the weighted quadrature norm, onto the empirical two-moment constraint set. Thus, the prescribed moments are exact for the selected quadrature rule, while continuum errors are quadrature errors of the corrected field. For decomposable high-dimensional linear operators, SDIFP combines affine moment correction with stochastic operator-subset sampling. With independent residual and derivative sampling and conditionally unbiased coefficient-gradient estimation, the resulting estimator is unbiased for the specified quadrature-based residual objective; the shared-subset fast mode is biased in general. SDIFP avoids tensor-product quadrature for moment enforcement, separates forward quadrature evaluation from the reverse-mode graph, and retains pointwise inference efficiency once the affine coefficients are fixed or precomputed.
item.dc:creator: Zhangyong Liang, Huanhuan Gao, Manyu Xiao

item.title: Unitary-Invariant Decomposition of Reducible Total Least Squares Core Problems
item.description: arXiv:2605.08091v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The analysis of a total least squares problem can be reduced to that of an associated core problem, which typically has lower dimension and improved solubility properties. Nevertheless, even a core problem may remain reducible, admitting further decomposition into irreducible component sub- problems with simpler structure and better analytical properties. We seek the finest decomposition under unitary transformations over C; for real data this decomposition can be strictly finer than the finest one under real orthogonal transformations. We split the data matrix into row blocks associated with the singular subspaces of the system matrix and consider the graph whose ver- tices are the blocks and whose edges correspond to nonzero cross-products. After preliminary splittings that make every nonzero cross-product a scalar multiple of a unitary matrix, we show that the components can be obtained directly from these blocks if and only if the covariance matrices along all cycles of the graph are scalar matrices. Otherwise, there is a chordless cycle whose covariance matrix is not a scalar matrix, and splitting the blocks on this cy- cle along the eigenspaces of the covariance matrix removes the obstruction without changing the decomposition. Based on these results, we propose a recursive strategy that finds all irreducible components over the complex field. The strategy is exact and theoretical rather than an efficient numerical algo- rithm; a small floating-point computation illustrates it. The results depend only on the core problem and therefore apply to general linear approximation problems AX B.
item.dc:creator: Sijia Yu, Bruno Carpentieri, Yan-Fei Jing

item.title: Floating-point autotuning with customized precisions
item.description: arXiv:2606.08339v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reduced-precision arithmetic offers significant opportunities to improve performance, memory usage, and energy efficiency in numerical applications, provided that numerical accuracy is preserved. This work investigates automated precision tuning through customized floating-point formats with user-defined exponent and significand sizes, enabling the emulation of emerging low-precision formats and the exploration of non-standard precision configurations within a unified mixed-precision framework. The proposed methodology, implemented in the PROMISE precision autotuning tool, combines numerical validation with a systematic search to generate program variants that satisfy user-defined accuracy requirements. To address the computational cost of this exploration, a containerized benchmarking framework supports parallel execution across multiple algorithms and parameter configurations. The approach is evaluated on a suite of numerical programs, including linear solvers and applications from the Rodinia benchmark. Results show that a substantial proportion of variables can be safely reduced to lower precision while preserving accuracy, indicating that standard double precision is often over-provisioned. These findings highlight the potential of automated precision tuning to derive efficient mixed-precision configurations tailored to application-specific accuracy requirements.
item.dc:creator: Xinye Chen, Fabienne J\'ez\'equel, Thibault Hilaire

item.title: Discovery of connectivity-trainability trade-off of IQP circuits for Hamiltonian optimization
item.description: arXiv:2606.24264v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial-time (IQP) circuits are promising candidates for near-term quantum computing due to the conjectured classical hardness of their sampling task and their shallow, highly parallelizable structure. Despite extensive studies of their complexity-theoretic properties, the role of circuit connectivity in their trainability as variational ansatze remains poorly understood. In this work, we present an investigation of IQP circuits for Hamiltonian optimization that traces a mechanistic chain linking circuit connectivity, entanglement generation, and gradient scaling: increasing connectivity drives the circuit output toward Haar-like statistics and volume-law entanglement, and this increase in entanglement is consistently associated with an exponential decay of the gradient variance and degraded optimization performance, while sparser architectures retain stable gradients at the cost of global expressibility and entanglement capacity. This connectivity-entanglement-gradient mechanism produces a nontrivial connectivity-trainability trade-off, demonstrating that effective IQP-based Hamiltonian optimization requires a balance between global expressibility and trainability rather than maximal expressivity alone. In particular, on our benchmarks, a circuit generating no entanglement already matches the optimization performance of more highly connected circuits, and a circular topology retains entanglement capacity while preserving trainability, making it a broadly effective choice among the architectures considered.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Physica Scripta (2026) Physica Scripta Physica Scripta
item.dc:creator: Quoc Chuong Nguyen, Dao Duy Tung, Vu Tuan Hai

item.title: Quasilinear multiplication in the Cayley-Dickson tower
item.description: arXiv:2609.11588v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Direct evaluation of the defining product of the Cayley-Dickson algebra $A_n$ of rank $N:=2^n$ over a unital commutative ring $R$ in which $2$ is invertible requires a quadratic number of arithmetic operations. This paper gives a uniform bilinear algorithm for multiplication in this algebra costing $O(N \log N)$ arithmetic operations in $R$ and $O(N)$ auxiliary storage when the doubling parameters of $A_n$ are units whose square roots lie in a fixed commutative coefficient algebra $S$ finitely generated as an $R$-module and admitting an $R$-linear map $\pi\colon S \to R$ with $\pi(1) = 1$. In particular, over $\mathbb{R}$ and every finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q}$ of odd characteristic, a quadratic field extension contains a square root of every possible doubling parameter, so the algorithm applies to every Cayley-Dickson tower over these fields, and the tensor rank of multiplication in $A_n$ over them is at most $(9n-21)2^n+28$ when $n\ge2$. When the top doubling parameter is a non-square, as in the standard real tower, the bound is $(9n-15)2^{n-1}+10$. To the author's knowledge, the algorithm presented in this paper is the first uniform subquadratic algorithm for multiplication in $A_n$. When $R=\mathbb{R}$ with every doubling parameter equal to $-1$, the real quasilinear schedule uses fewer total arithmetic operations than both direct multiplication and a uniform algorithm of Cariow-Cariowa for $n\ge4$. An implementation for the standard real tower is available in the MIT-licensed C11 library fastCD, with a NumPy-backed Python interface. In single-core benchmarks against direct multiplication and the uniform Cariow-Cariowa method, the quasilinear implementation had the lowest mean time of the three at every tested dimension $N\ge32$, for both single and batched products, and was over $17$ times faster than direct multiplication at $N=1024$.
item.dc:creator: Harrison Lemley

item.title: Verified Linear Programming via Tolerance-Aware Precision Boosting
item.description: arXiv:2609.11721v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Linear programming plays a fundamental role in computer science, with applications in optimization, formal verification, SMT solving, and numerous other domains. When exactness guarantees are required, numerical inaccuracies arising from floating-point arithmetic can compromise soundness, whereas exact rational arithmetic often incurs significant computational overhead. In this paper, we investigate the numerical stability of the simplex algorithm and establish conditions under which a precision-boosting floating-point implementation provably produces the same pivot decisions and final basis as an exact rational implementation, from which the final result is reconstructed and certified exactly. Our analysis shows that correctness depends on both arithmetic precision and a careful handling of numerical tolerances. Based on these results, we develop a tolerance-aware, precision-boosting simplex algorithm with formal correctness guarantees. Finally, we introduce a delta-complete termination criterion that allows the algorithm to terminate once certified upper and lower bounds on the optimal objective differ by at most a user-specified threshold delta, providing a certified, user-controlled optimality gap.
item.dc:creator: Ernesto Casablanca, Martin Sidaway, Sadegh Soudjani, Paolo Zuliani
